scenarios.title: CUI Vault Unauthorized Access Tabletop
scenarios.summary: A user account shows anomalous access to the Windows Server 2025 CUI Vault from an unusual location or time window. Tests detection, identity escalation, account disablement, privileged access review, log preservation, customer notification, and DoD cyber incident reporting decision.
scenarios.narrative: At 02:14 local time, the SOC observes a successful interactive logon to the customer's single-tenant CUI Vault using a service account that normally only runs scheduled tasks. The source IP geolocates outside the United States. Within minutes, audit logs show bulk access to a CUI folder. The exercise tests whether the customer's incident response capability detects the event, escalates correctly, contains the access, preserves evidence, and applies the DFARS 252.204-7012 72-hour reporting decision criteria.
scenarios.defaultRoe: Simulation only. No real destructive activity. No live CUI exposure. All decisions documented in writing. The facilitator may pause for clarification but should not coach. Each inject must be acknowledged within 5 minutes; expected actions must be decided within posted timeframes. Mobile devices may be used for reference only; no live system commands during the exercise.

injectsJson.prompt: User reports they cannot access the CUI Vault from their office workstation. Helpdesk creates a ticket with priority TBD.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Open formal incident ticket; classify priority; route to security lead.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Ticket opened within 5 minutes; classified at minimum P3.

injectsJson.prompt: SIEM alerts on 7 failed admin login attempts to the vault (RDP) from IP 198.51.100.42 (Brazil) over 90 seconds.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Escalate to security lead; preserve current logs; begin source IP analysis.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Escalation within 15 minutes; explicit log preservation order issued.

injectsJson.prompt: Successful interactive logon from the same IP using service account 'svc-vault-admin'. SSH session active. Account has Backup Operator privileges.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Disable service account; capture session evidence; review privileged access records.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Account disabled within 10 minutes of inject; session terminated; evidence preservation documented.

injectsJson.prompt: Audit logs show 1.2 GB of CUI files accessed in bulk by the suspect session; rsync process detected initiating outbound transfer.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Determine potential CUI exposure scope; isolate vault network segment; notify customer security lead.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Scoping decision within 15 minutes; customer security lead reached within 30 minutes; isolation order issued.

injectsJson.prompt: Customer Program Manager asks: must DoD be notified within 72 hours per DFARS 252.204-7012(c)? The 72-hour clock starts when?
injectsJson.expectedAction: Apply reporting decision criteria; consult contract program officer; identify DC3/DCISE submission path; document the 72-hour clock anchor.
injectsJson.passCriteria: 72-hour clock acknowledged with explicit anchor time; reporting decision documented within 30 minutes; DIBNet/DC3 submission path identified.

injectsJson.prompt: Vault is restored from the last known-good snapshot; root cause not yet identified; the suspect IP is now in deny-list.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Decide recovery acceptance; flag POA&M item for forensic completion; capture lessons learned for AAR.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Recovery decision documented; POA&M entry initiated with owner and target date; AAR scheduled.

scenarios.title: CUI Vault Exfiltration Indicator Tabletop
scenarios.summary: Audit logs indicate a user accessed multiple CUI files and attempted unusual outbound transfer activity. Tests containment, evidence preservation, scoping affected CUI, reporting decision, contract officer notification path, and DIBNet/DoD reporting procedure.
scenarios.narrative: DLP alerts indicate an authorized user 'j.smith' has downloaded an unusually large volume of CUI files in the past hour and the workstation is now exhibiting outbound HTTPS traffic to an unfamiliar domain. The exercise tests whether the customer can contain the suspected exfiltration, preserve forensic evidence, scope the affected CUI, decide on contract officer and DC3/DCISE notification, and document the reporting determination.
scenarios.defaultRoe: Simulation only. No real destructive activity. No live CUI exposure. All decisions documented in writing. Network operations team must not actually quarantine production endpoints during the exercise.

injectsJson.prompt: DLP system alerts: user 'j.smith' downloaded 47 CUI files in the past 60 minutes; outbound HTTPS to unknown domain 'storage-13.relay.example.com'.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Open incident ticket at P1; assign incident commander; preserve DLP and proxy logs.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Ticket opened at P1 within 5 minutes; IC named; log preservation order issued.

injectsJson.prompt: Network telemetry shows 850 MB upload to the unknown domain over TLS; transfer ongoing.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Decision: terminate user session and isolate endpoint; capture pre-isolation memory image if feasible.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Session termination decision within 5 minutes; isolation order issued; evidence preservation explicit.

injectsJson.prompt: Endpoint isolated from network; user account session revoked; user has been contacted by HR for interview.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Confirm containment; review whether other endpoints used the same credentials; rotate dependent secrets.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Containment confirmation documented; lateral-access review initiated; dependent secrets identified for rotation.

injectsJson.prompt: Affected CUI files identified; preliminary scoping = 12 GB across 3 contract programs (Program Alpha, Beta, Delta).
injectsJson.expectedAction: Map affected files to contract programs; identify per-contract reporting obligations; flag whether any files contain ITAR/export-controlled material.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Per-program impact identified within 15 minutes; ITAR/export-control flag explicitly addressed.

injectsJson.prompt: Contract officer asks for written notification by end of day. Does DFARS 252.204-7012 require DC3/DCISE submission?
injectsJson.expectedAction: Apply reporting decision criteria; draft contract officer notification; identify DC3/DCISE submission path and 72-hour clock anchor.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Reporting decision documented within 30 minutes; 72-hour clock anchored explicitly; written notification drafted.

injectsJson.prompt: Forensic image of endpoint preserved with chain of custody; recovery options being evaluated; AAR scheduling pending.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Confirm chain-of-custody documentation; decide recovery posture; schedule AAR; capture lessons learned.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Chain-of-custody confirmed in writing; recovery decision made; AAR scheduled within 14 days.

scenarios.title: Endpoint Ransomware with CUI Vault Adjacency Tabletop
scenarios.summary: A customer workstation used to access the CUI Vault is suspected of ransomware compromise. Tests boundary determination (in/out of CMMC scope), session revocation, vault isolation, credential rotation, CUI exposure analysis, and recovery and backup validation.
scenarios.narrative: EDR triggers a ransomware behavioral signature on workstation WS-007. The user assigned to WS-007 has accessed the CUI Vault within the last 24 hours. The tabletop tests whether the customer can quickly determine the CMMC boundary implications, prevent lateral spread to the vault, rotate credentials touched by WS-007, scope CUI exposure, and validate backup integrity prior to recovery.
scenarios.defaultRoe: Simulation only. EDR demo events are safe. No actual file encryption performed. Backup restoration is discussed only; no production restore actions taken.

injectsJson.prompt: EDR alert on WS-007: ransomware behavioral signature; encrypted file extension '.lockbit3' observed in user document folder.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Open P1 incident; assign IC; isolate WS-007 from network; preserve EDR alert evidence.
injectsJson.passCriteria: P1 ticket within 5 minutes; isolation order within 10 minutes; evidence preserved.

injectsJson.prompt: Determine: is WS-007 inside or outside the CMMC assessment boundary as documented in the SSP?
injectsJson.expectedAction: Consult SSP boundary statement; document determination; if in-scope, apply CMMC IR procedures fully.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Boundary determination documented in writing within 10 minutes with reference to SSP section.

injectsJson.prompt: Vault session for the WS-007 user is still active. Decide whether to revoke immediately.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Revoke active vault session; document decision; if active CUI access in progress, capture session details first.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Session revocation decision documented within 5 minutes; capture-then-revoke order followed if applicable.

injectsJson.prompt: Credential rotation: should service account credentials accessed from WS-007 in the last 30 days be rotated?
injectsJson.expectedAction: Identify credentials accessed from WS-007; initiate rotation; document scope.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Credential scope identified within 15 minutes; rotation initiated for in-scope creds.

injectsJson.prompt: CUI exposure analysis: any CUI files the WS-007 user opened in last 24 hours that may now be in attacker hands?
injectsJson.expectedAction: Enumerate accessed CUI files; cross-reference with last-24h vault audit log; scope notification obligations.
injectsJson.passCriteria: File enumeration completed; notification scope documented within 30 minutes.

injectsJson.prompt: Backup restore decision: validate backup integrity before any restore action; confirm RPO acceptable per BCP.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Validate backup integrity (hash check / restore-to-test); confirm RPO; decide restore source.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Backup integrity confirmed before restore decision; RPO documented; restore source recorded.

injectsJson.prompt: Recovery complete; AAR scheduling and corrective action register opened.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Confirm recovery success; populate corrective action register with findings; schedule AAR.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Recovery confirmed; CAR populated with at least 2 findings; AAR scheduled.

scenarios.title: Azure Gov Tenant Service Anomaly Tabletop
scenarios.summary: Azure Defender, Windows Event Viewer, or vault monitoring identifies suspicious process execution, failed logons, or privilege escalation activity. Tests MacTech/customer shared responsibility, escalation to MacTech support, evidence collection, recovery from known-good configuration, and service continuity.
scenarios.narrative: Azure Defender for Servers raises an alert on the customer's Windows Server 2025 vault VM in their Azure Gov tenant: a child process has been spawned by lsass.exe that does not match the Microsoft-signed baseline. The tabletop tests how the customer and MacTech support coordinate per the Shared Responsibility Matrix, what evidence each party owns, and how recovery is achieved without breaking the assessment boundary.
scenarios.defaultRoe: Simulation only. MacTech support participation is in-band as a participant, not a live escalation channel. All system commands are notional.

injectsJson.prompt: Azure Defender alert: 'Suspicious process spawned by lsass.exe' on Windows Server 2025 vault VM in Azure Gov tenant. Severity High.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Open P1 incident; assign IC; preserve Defender alert; freeze the VM image (snapshot) before any remediation.
injectsJson.passCriteria: P1 ticket within 5 minutes; IC named; pre-remediation snapshot taken; Defender alert preserved.

injectsJson.prompt: Determine: is this a MacTech-platform issue or a customer-tenant issue per the Shared Responsibility Matrix?
injectsJson.expectedAction: Consult SRM; classify the alert per the responsibility column; document the call.
injectsJson.passCriteria: SRM classification documented in writing within 10 minutes.

injectsJson.prompt: Escalate to MacTech support; capture initial evidence (Windows Event IDs 4688 process create, 4624 logon, 4672 special privileges).
injectsJson.expectedAction: Open MacTech support case; share Event IDs and timestamps; agree on collection scope and timing.
injectsJson.passCriteria: MacTech case opened with case number; event evidence shared; collection scope agreed.

injectsJson.prompt: Customer security lead requests evidence package: confirm what MacTech provides (vault-side telemetry) vs. what customer must collect (workstation-side, identity tenant).
injectsJson.expectedAction: Walk through SRM evidence columns; confirm collection ownership for each item; document split.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Per-item evidence ownership documented; no item left unowned.

injectsJson.prompt: Recovery: restore VM from a known-good configuration baseline; validate post-restore baseline.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Identify last validated baseline; perform restore (notional); validate against CIS/STIG baseline.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Baseline source documented; restore decision recorded; post-restore validation step planned.

injectsJson.prompt: Service continuity: confirm vault is available to authorized users; AAR scheduled.
injectsJson.expectedAction: Smoke-test vault availability for authorized users; capture downtime metric; schedule AAR.
injectsJson.passCriteria: Availability confirmed; downtime metric captured; AAR scheduled.
